currentContext.expansion: The bundle carries no named plant, line or capacity-addition project with a commissioning or ramp timeline. What the Company does state is its existing scale: it has the largest capacity for manufacturing of synthetic leather in the domestic organised segment, with annual production capacity of 48.60 Million linear meters of PVC coated fabric and 5.00 Million Linear meter of PU coated fabric, and it manufactures more than 400 variants of artificial leather from PVC polymer. risks.risk: Raw material availability and supply reliability
risks.note: Management lists as threats that some raw material is not available locally, increasing cost and affecting competitiveness, and that supply of raw material is irregular; increases in raw material prices are also named among the risks and concerns the Company continuously monitors.

Unfavourable foreign exchange rate fluctuation is listed as a threat and foreign exchange fluctuation is named among the risks and concerns the Company continuously monitors - material for a business whose overseas subsidiaries drove a significant part of the year's sales increase.

The Company deals only in one segment - manufacturing and sale of PU/PVC synthetic leather - and reports a single reportable segment, so there is no internal diversification to absorb a demand or pricing shock in artificial leather.
Geographical concentration is explicitly named in the MD&A Risks and Concerns list among the risks the Company monitors, alongside macro-economic factors.

Increase in competition is listed as a threat, as is increase in logistics cost; both bear directly on realisations and on landed cost competitiveness in a business whose material competes on being a cheaper alternative to natural leather.

risks.risk: Product sustainability - non-biodegradability and the innovation race
risks.note: Non-biodegradability of synthetic leather is listed as a threat. The BRSR materiality table adds that failure to innovate and adapt to changing sustainability trends may reduce market competitiveness and customer preference, that increasing regulatory requirements on product sustainability and chemicals may create compliance risks, and that inability to meet customer expectations for sustainable products may cost business opportunities - relevant given the market's shift to water-based PU, solvent-free coatings and bio-based feedstocks.

risks.risk: Climate, emissions and energy transition risk
risks.note: The Company flags that customer and regulatory expectations may increase compliance and operational costs, that failure to reduce emissions may result in reputational risks, reduced market access and loss of business opportunities, and that physical climate risks such as extreme weather events may disrupt operations and supply chains. On energy it flags that rising energy prices and dependence on conventional energy sources may increase operating costs and transition risks, that energy supply disruptions can affect production continuity and operational efficiency, and that increasing regulatory requirements related to energy efficiency and climate change may result in additional compliance obligations.

risks.risk: Water and waste - operational continuity and compliance
risks.note: Water scarcity, declining groundwater levels and climate change may impact water availability for operations; increasing water costs and regulatory requirements may increase operational expenses; inefficient water use or inadequate wastewater management may result in environmental impacts, compliance risks and reputational damage; and water-related disruptions may affect production continuity. On waste, improper handling, storage or disposal may result in environmental pollution, regulatory penalties and reputational damage.

Changes in government policy and legislation are named among the risks the Company monitors, and management separately lists lack of poor policies for the specific development of the sector as a threat. Risks are overseen under a Risk Management Policy reviewed by the Audit and Risk Management Committee, with insurance policies taken to mitigate other risks.

one-line thesis: Mayur Uniquoters delivered a blowout Q4FY26 with PAT up 73% YoY (standalone), driven by a structural shift toward high-margin automotive exports (up 50% YoY) and favorable FX realization. financial scorecard: Revenue (Standalone): INR 260.55 Cr (+22% YoY); Revenue (Consol): INR 273.35 Cr (+9% YoY). EBITDA Margin: ~31% (Q4, elevated by mix/FX). PAT (Standalone): INR 60.71 Cr (+73% YoY); PAT (Consol): INR 59.43 Cr (+43% YoY). Order Book: Not disclosed (projection-based supply). Net Debt: Not explicitly stated; Capex guided at INR 50 Cr (India) + potential INR 300 Cr (Global). One-offs: FX gain of ~INR 3 Cr in Q4 (part of INR 30 Cr annual gain reported in Other Income); Employee expenses spiked INR 3 Cr due to new labor code provisions.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Domestic 8-10%, Export 15-20% (Value terms). Margin: 25-30% EBITDA range expected. Order Inflow: Strong projections from existing auto platforms; Ford platform expansion ongoing. Capex: INR 50 Cr for new coating line in existing facility (commissioning by Dec 2026); INR 300 Cr reserved for future global location (Mexico/other).
order book & pipeline: No fixed order book; business runs on monthly volume projections from OEMs. Export auto OEM revenue for FY26 was INR 290 Cr vs INR 194 Cr in FY25 (+50%).
segment / subsidiary detail: Q4 Breakdown (Standalone): Export OEM INR 88 Cr; Auto OEM Domestic INR 55 Cr; Replacement INR 41 Cr; Footwear INR 48 Cr; Export General INR 21 Cr; Furnishing INR 5 Cr. Full Year Export Auto grew 50% to INR 290 Cr. PU business remains muted (FY26 rev INR 27 Cr).
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion of Ford platforms; penetration in European/US marine and furnishing segments; potential greenfield global plant (INR 300 Cr) to bypass tariffs/logistics.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 margin expansion driven by: 1) Higher export mix (42.5% of total, rising); 2) FX gains on dollar-denominated auto contracts; 3) Operating efficiency (OE) improvements; 4) Lower freight/maintenance costs. Raw material (PVC paste/Yarn) prices rose in March but availability is stable; price hikes passed to customers with 1-2 month lag.
capex / expansion: INR 50 Cr for new coating line in existing facility (adds ~5 lakh meters/month capacity, est. INR 120-150 Cr revenue potential). Commissioning expected by Dec 2026. Global plant capex (INR 300 Cr) is contingent on location finalization.
capital allocation: Focus on organic capacity expansion within existing footprint to minimize capex; evaluating global location for strategic de-risking; CSR initiatives (45k+ plants, education/health).
risks & watch-items: Volatility in crude/PVC prices; Geopolitical tensions impacting freight/logistics (Middle East/Europe); Labor code cost inflation; Customer concentration in auto OEMs; FX reversal risk.
management quality / tone: Confident on structural margin re-rating (25-30% vs historical 24-25%); Conservative on guiding specific quarterly numbers but firm on annual growth trajectories; Transparent on FX and labor code impacts.
non-obvious takeaways: The margin jump to 31% is not just cyclical but structural due to the mix shift to auto exports (50% growth) which are dollar-priced and higher margin. The INR 3 Cr Q4 FX gain is small relative to the operational leverage gained from the export mix. Employee cost spike is a one-time regulatory adjustment (new labor codes) rather than aggressive hiring.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global synthetic leather market estimated at USD 49.10 billion in 2025 and projected to reach around USD 103.91 billion by 2035, a CAGR of approximately 7.78 percent between 2026 and 2035
- Asia Pacific synthetic leather market estimated at USD 21.07 billion in 2025 and projected to reach around USD 45.93 billion by 2035 at a CAGR of approximately 8.1 percent, with India, China and South Korea the principal growth drivers; Asia Pacific holds over 43 percent of global value
- Automotive is expected to be the fastest-growing application at a 13.2% CAGR, supported by rapid expansion of electric vehicles and premium interior customization programs
- Footwear remains the largest application by revenue share at over 31 percent, with rising footwear production in China, India, Vietnam and Indonesia driving substitution into synthetic material
- PU synthetic leather holds the largest product share at over 53 percent, with innovation concentrated in water-based PU systems, solvent-free coatings, microfiber structures and bio-based feedstocks
- Rising demand for animal-free and sustainable products is a major driver, with synthetic leather positioned as a cheaper alternative to natural leather with good aesthetic quality
- Low-VOC and odour-controlled materials meeting strict cabin air quality standards are being pulled by automotive and premium footwear customers
- Profit after tax improved on effective cost savings plans, increase in sales price and a significant increase in sales in overseas subsidiaries, with management stating the subsidiaries contributed significantly to consolidated revenue
- Headwinds management flags: unfavourable foreign exchange rate fluctuations, some raw material not available locally which increases cost and affects competitiveness, and irregular supply of raw material

margins.body: Q4 margin expansion driven by: 1) Higher export mix (42.5% of total, rising); 2) FX gains on dollar-denominated auto contracts; 3) Operating efficiency (OE) improvements; 4) Lower freight/maintenance costs. Raw material (PVC paste/Yarn) prices rose in March but availability is stable; price hikes passed to customers with 1-2 month lag.
